This violates checks-effects-interactions pattern. An attacker can create a contract with a receive() function that re-enters claimReward() multiple times before the state is updated, draining the reward pool.
attack_strategy: 1. Create an attacker contract that holds MVK tokens. 2. Generate rewards by selling tokens (which adds ETH to reward pool). 3. Call claimReward() from the attacker contract. 4. In the receive() function, re-enter claimReward() multiple times before the state update occurs. 5. Withdraw stolen ETH.
step_by_step_plan: 1. Impersonate owner to initialize contract and set parameters. 2. Transfer tokens to attacker contract. 3. Sell tokens to generate reward pool ETH. 4. Execute reentrancy attack via claimReward(). 5. Verify attacker balance increased.
